reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes BitClub as a way to earn Bitcoin through mining-pool shares and referral activity, claiming payments tied to participant and recruit purchases and inviting viewers to join for a $99 fee. The records do not verify mining activity, actual payouts, or what occurs after joining.

citations.quote: when you first join everyone is called a minor. As soon as you sponsor 5 miners so that's 5 people here the people in blue and they each sponsor 2 miners themselves
you can receive an additional income from the people in your team that are also receiving binary bonuses
If someone buys a $500 dollar share in mining pool 1 in mining pool two you receive one credit.
were earning everyday profits from the bitcoin mining

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present every illustrated payout as available to every viewer. He states that binary cycles are capped within a 24-hour period, that reaching Builder requires sponsorship and organizational volume, and that keeping Pro Builder status requires new monthly volume. These are consequential qualifications, not an unconditional earnings promise. The presentation deserves scrutiny, but its stated limits support reading it as an explanation of contingent plan rules rather than proof of deception.

citations.quote: you can only have a maximum of 4 cycles within the 24 hour period
you need to do is when you first join everyone is called a minor. As soon as you sponsor 5 miners
once you're qualified you'll maintain that qualification, providing every month you get $10,000 worth

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's mining-share and daily-profit quotes identify claims, not evidence that a payout occurred or that the speaker guaranteed one. Its recruitment quote likewise describes a qualification hurdle; it does not establish that five recruits will materialize. The limits on cycles matter when interpreting the earnings examples: the speaker expressly places a ceiling on that particular bonus. A case based on unverified outcomes cannot treat the advertised examples as verified outcomes either.

citations.quote: were earning everyday profits from the bitcoin mining
you can only have a maximum of 4 cycles within the 24 hour period

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Caps and qualification hurdles are not risk warnings. They specify how participants can earn from a recruitment structure: the speaker says members get paid for introducing people, describes commissions on team members' purchases, and urges interested viewers to contact their inviter about joining. Nothing in the cited limits verifies mining profits or removes the promotional purpose.

citations.quote: Just like any referral network, we get paid introducing other people.
you personally earn a direct commission of 10 percent on whatever they purchase
get back to them if you're interested in joining

opening.argument: Judge, this is structured as a walkthrough of a compensation plan. The speaker announces that he will take viewers through each commission type, then explains what a left and right team mean and how credits are matched. He closes by inviting viewers to replay the recording and pause where needed. That instructional sequence gives the video an operational purpose: explaining stated rules. The explanation may be promotional, but promotion alone does not establish that the described system is fraudulent.

citations.quote: I will further on in this presentation take you through each one of those.
in a binary plan you have a left team and a right team
I encourage you to go back play the recording stop it whenever you need to

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes sponsorship and matching-bonus rules, but those are precisely the rules this walkthrough explains. A description of what participants would receive if others join or cycle does not show that anyone actually received it. Nor does the quoted claim about mining profits independently substantiate the claim. The question is what this video establishes, and a plan explanation establishes the speaker's account of the plan, not its real-world performance.

citations.quote: you can receive an additional income from the people in your team that are also receiving binary bonuses
were earning everyday profits from the bitcoin mining

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough format does not make this detached instruction. The speaker identifies himself with the network, says participants get paid for introductions, and directs interested viewers back to whoever invited them. The detailed rules teach viewers how to participate in the promoted recruitment and purchase structure; they do not independently verify its mining or payouts.

citations.quote: My name's Simon Patmore from the BITclub Network team.
Just like any referral network, we get paid introducing other people.
get back to them if you're interested in joining

opening.argument: Judge, the stated offer connects a membership fee and purchases of mining-pool shares to a disclosed referral compensation plan. The speaker gives the fee, a share-price example, and a direct-commission example rather than concealing that referrals are paid. That supports reading the video as a commercial pitch whose terms require evaluation, not as evidence by itself that viewers' money is taken without a service. The supplied presentation shows no completed purchase or failed payout, and its claims should not be mistaken for independent proof of either success or fraud.

citations.quote: there is a one of membership fee of $99
If someone buys a $500 dollar share in mining pool 1 in mining pool two you receive one credit.
if they buy a five hundred dollar share in pool number one you get ten percent that's a fifty dollar commission

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly notes the fee, shares, recruitment, and lack of verified mining or payouts. But lack of verification cuts both ways: its cited statements do not demonstrate that a share was undelivered or a promised payment withheld. The presentation openly connects bonuses to purchases and team activity. The judge can recognize the commercial incentive without treating the unverified operation of the service as a proven fraudulent outcome.

citations.quote: you personally earn a direct commission of 10 percent on whatever they purchase
you can receive an additional income from the people in your team that are also receiving binary bonuses

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is the promoted mechanism, not proof of a completed loss. The speaker ties credits to purchases, bonuses to recruits' cycles, and higher ranks to organizational volume. He also invites interested viewers to join through their inviter. Disclosing those terms does not turn a recruitment-driven earnings pitch with unverified mining returns into ordinary retail commerce.
